extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners building/evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning benchmarks and Chain-of-Thought evaluation (ML/NLP researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating synthetic chained math reasoning benchmarks (Scheherazade) to measure Chain-of-Thought reasoning in LLMs, and the experimental protocol for comparing models across chain lengths and chaining techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark differentiation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks should be able to distinguish reasoning capabilities of competing LLMs, even as models approach saturation on existing datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation: existing benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K) have become less discriminative as models reach >94% accuracy. New benchmarks must produce problems that reveal remaining reasoning differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase complexity via logical chaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Create composite problems by logically chaining multiple base benchmark problems together so that solving later problems depends on solving earlier ones (nested dependencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheherazade chains benchmarks using conditional branching to form nested reasoning tasks; chaining increases nesting and thus reasoning complexity as chain length grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward chaining vs backward chaining distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward chaining: problems linked so the composite can be solved sequentially in written order. Backward chaining: problems earlier require context from later problems, forcing reverse reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backward chaining introduces added complexity because it forces models to reason in reverse at each step; the paper demonstrates different model behaviours on forward vs backward chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized branching to prevent memorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce conditional branching and randomness between questions so models cannot memorize branch sequences and must reason instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomly selected if-then-else branches and randomized choices of r_i constructs between subsequent questions; randomness ensures format memorization is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support arbitrary ordering and chain length generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Chaining technique should generalize to any chain length and permit arbitrary permutations of component problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheherazade allows any permutation of problems and both chaining techniques generalize to any length n; evaluation spans lengths 2 through 10 in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of conditional if-then-else structure for chaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Chain problems by inserting branching 'if then else' statements linking conclusions of one problem to premises of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template examples: Ac => B1 ∧ ¬Ac => B'1; concatenation of premises and conclusions constructs the composite textual question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong-branch property (need for wrong conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each base problem must include a wrong conclusion and an alternate first premise so that selecting the wrong branch yields an incorrect conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any question Q, Q'1 has the property that Q'1 ⇏ Qc, meaning if the wrong branch is taken the corresponding premise yields an incorrect conclusion; this enables meaningful branching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing constraints for base benchmark set
rubrics_metrics.description: The starting set of benchmarks must satisfy specific constraints: no pronouns, unique names/variables across benchmarks, and an incorrect conclusion for each problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constraints reduce ambiguity when chaining; some preprocessing can be automated but manual cleanup may be required (limitation noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation power / combinatoric coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how many distinct chained problems can be generated from N starting problems and chain lengths l using the technique's randomness and two chaining modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper gives formula: total number = 2 · Σ_{l=2}^{?} 2^{l−1} · N!/(N−l)!. Example: with N=50, technique can generate ≈ 5.64·10^79 different problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sampling protocol (chain lengths and sample sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models across multiple chain lengths and both chaining techniques with sufficiently large random samples per length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the paper: for each model (except o1-preview) evaluate 1000 randomly generated forward and 1000 backward problems per length for lengths 2–10 (9000 forward+9000 backward total); o1-preview evaluated on 200 per length per technique. This yields robust statistics across lengths and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary metrics: raw accuracy and normalized accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw accuracy (fraction correct) per chain length and chaining technique; also report accuracy normalized to accuracy on length-1 (original) problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalized accuracy = accuracy_at_length_l / accuracy_at_length_1; normalization highlights relative degradation with chain length and isolates effects beyond base problem difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: forward vs backward difficulty patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark analysis should compare forward and backward chaining trends and note model-specific differences (e.g., some models decline more on backward chains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed: most models decline rapidly on backward chains; o1-preview maintained stronger backward reasoning. Consider model token-prediction nature as an explanation for forward advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error taxonomy for incorrect outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify incorrect model outputs into semantic misunderstanding errors, wrong path errors, false negatives, and other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy is used to analyze failure modes; sampling and manual labeling (e.g., 40 incorrect outputs per model per technique) can reveal dominant error types and guide improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic misunderstanding errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors where the model produces an answer indicating a misunderstanding of the question, including misunderstanding conditions or interpreting quantities incorrectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: misinterpreting tip calculation (40/1.25 vs 40×1.25) or assuming conditional statements are true and working backwards to fit premises to conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong path errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors where the model solved an intermediate correctly but then followed the wrong conditional branch, skipped a step, or hallucinated a non-existent alternative path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes hallucinated 'Alternative Exploration' where the model tweaks numbers to fit a desired answer; indicates control-flow tracking problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: False negatives due to answer extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where the evaluation/extraction system fails to detect a correct answer because the model's output format differs or the model refutes a branch instead of explicitly giving the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports ~3.75% of errors due to false negatives; robust answer extraction/parsing is necessary to avoid underestimating performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other and rare failure modes (e.g., infinite loops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture miscellaneous error types that don't fit taxonomy; note rare model-specific behaviors such as output runaway/infinite-loop style repetitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: GPT-4o sometimes produced extremely long repeated outputs (~100k characters) effectively hitting output limits; such behaviours should be detected and handled in evaluation harnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling-based error analysis procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform manual analysis on a random subset of incorrect answers to quantify error categories and better understand failure modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper sampled 40 incorrect answers per model (20 forward, 20 backward) for manual categorization; such sampling helps reveal dominant error types and model-specific patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for preventing trivial solutions (avoid format memorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that chained problems, branching choices, and randomization prevent models from exploiting superficial patterns or memorized sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomized branching, alternate premises/conclusions, and permutations of problem ordering to force genuine reasoning rather than pattern matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and preprocessing overhead acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about limitations: answer extraction false negatives, preprocessing requirements for base dataset, and potential manual cleanup needed to meet chaining constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State measured impact (e.g., 3.75% false negatives), and document the base-problem constraints (no pronouns, unique names, wrong conclusions) and the consequent overhead when applying the method to new datasets.
